newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
OVER 200 DEVOTEES BURNT TO DEATH IN ORISSA TOWN

Over 200 people were killed and 500 injured when a devastating fire swept through a number of temporary sheds constructed for a religious conference in Baripada, Orissa. Officials said over 5,000 devotees attending a state level three-day conference were trapped when the sheds caught fire.
The Economic Times
SIEMENS INTO HUGE REVAMP TO MAKE GOOD LOSSES

Siemens, the 11.86 billion rupee Indian affiliate of the German multinational, embarked upon a major restructuring programme aimed at stemming losses. This followed a substantial slowdown in demand for some of its major products. The programme included curtailing fresh investments on a large scale, retrenching work force, shedding unproductive assets and minimising essential expenses.
JARDINE UPGRADES INDIA TO OVERWEIGHT CATEGORY

Jardine Fleming assigned overweight category to India after a gap of more than eight months, upgrading it from the neutral category. It felt fears of a recession were unwarranted, although the economy may go through a minor slowdown in the current fiscal. Jardine expected GDP growth in the current financial year to be 5.9 percent which was expected to jump to 6.4 percent in 1997/98 (March-April). This would be led by higher industrial production growth of 9.3 percent in 1997/98, up from 7.6 percent.
Financial Express
ESSAR STEEL IN $100-M CREDIT DEAL WITH US FIRM

Essar Steel would go in for an up front credit arrangement of $100 million with the $1.8 billion U.S.-based Commercial Metal Corporation's trading arm based in Switzerland, for the export of its hot-rolled coils. This was said to be the largest corporate banking deal of its kind.
IMPORT DUTY ON CRUDE MAY BE CUT TO 20 PCT

The Finance Ministry was exploring the option of reducing import duty on crude oil from 25 percent to around 20 percent. If approved, this would be announced in the Budget, sources said. This stemmed from the increasing consumption of petroleum products. It was presently estimated at seven percent per annum and would more than offset a marginal cut in the import duty of crude.
INFLATION TOUCHES 63 WEEK HIGH

The annual rate of inflation jumped to touch a 63-week high of eight percent for the week ended February 8, 1997. Annual inflation (provisional-over-final) went up by 0.26 percent points to 7.99 percent as against 7.73 percent in the previous week. The wholesale price index for all commodities (base 1981- 82 = 100) also rose by 0.3 percent to 321.5 compared to 320.6 for the previous week.
The Economic Times
RAILWAYS NOT TO SPARE LOW RATED COMMODITIES

The Railway Minister decided to marginally raise passenger and freight tariff. The Railway budget preparation exercise suggested a 5-10 percent freight rate hike. It also incorporated reclassification of goods traffic. This would cover even low rated commodities including sugar, salt for common consumption, oil cakes for exports, kerosene, vegetables and fruits. These commodities would be spared the proposed freight hike but would be paying slightly higher tariff.
Business Standard
BOURSE REGULATOR TO WATCH MERCHANT BANK STAFF

For the first time ever, the stock market regulator (SEBI) would prepare a database on all personnel in merchant banking outfits to keep a close tab on them. The move was aimed at monitoring the activities of every individual involved in merchant banking as defined under the SEBI regulations. The regulator expected the bulk of the database to be completed within a month or 45 days.
HUGHES ISPAT SET TO PLACE ORDER ON ALCATEL

Hughes Ispat was close to a $480 million telecommunication equipment supply deal, the first by a basic services licensee in the country, with the French telecom major Alcatel. Hughes Ispat, the letter of intent (LoI) holder for providing basic telecom services in Maharashtra, is a 51:49 joint venture of the Mittals, promoters of steel maker Nippon Denro Ispat, and Hughes Corp of the U.S. The supply would be limited to telephone exchanges and transmission equipment.
GENERAL INSURANCE CORP MAY SHED 24 PCT IN SUBSIDIARIES

The government was expected to initiate reforms in general insurance by moving towards delinking General Insurance Corporation's (GIC) four subsidiaries. It was likely to offer 24 percent of GIC's stake in each of the subsidiaries - Oriental Insurance, National Insurance, New India Assurance and United India Insurance - to private investors.
The Observer
RED TAPE SET TO STYMIE FOREIGN TAKEOVER MOVES

The government was taking all possible measures to check hostile takeovers of domestic firms by foreign investors. A recent inter-ministerial meeting decided to subject the takeover proposals of foreign investors to a stringent approval system. The meeting also outlined the role of various government departments with regard to takeover applications.
Business Line
FIVE PCT HIKE IN INTERNATIONAL AIR FARES PERMITTED

The government permitted international carriers operating from India, including the national carriers, to raise their air fares by five percent for the second time this year. The hike was permitted to offset the rising price of aviation turbine fuel. This, however, was less than the IATA recommendation to revise fares by 10 percent from India. The government had approved a five percent increase in fares on the India-Gulf sector in January, which was carried out to keep pace with annual worldwide inflation.
